title: The influence of biographical factors on vocational training: a comparison of individuals with ADHD in a retrospective-prospective study
summary: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder is a common neurodevelopmental condition that can affect both children and adults. The transition from adolescent healthcare services to adult healthcare services can be challenging for many affected individuals. The aim of this study is to identify factors associated with successful occupational outcomes and to determine which forms of support are most helpful during this transition. A total of 350 to 400 adults will participate in a standardized interview. In addition, follow-up questionnaires will be conducted. The results are intended to improve healthcare services and support for individuals with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder during the transition to adulthood.

interventions.name: Interviews comprising 179 items and a further 15 items in follow-up questionnaires (to be evaluated), with the aim of including 350–400 participants; the time required is a good 40 minutes per participant

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Physician-diagnosed attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
• Age ≥ 15 years
• Ability to participate independently in a standardized interview of approximately 40 minutes
• Sufficient German language skills to understand study procedures and questionnaires
• Written informed consent to participate in the study
• Willingness to participate in follow-up assessments
Exclusion criteria:
• Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
• Insufficient German language proficiency for completion of the interview
• No confirmed ADHD diagnosis
• Missing or incomplete informed consent
• Withdrawal from the study before completion of essential study procedures
